newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra to release Wallis report in April.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra to release Wallis report in April.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday he expected to release the government's financial system inquiry report sometime in the week starting April 7.

"I expect that I'll be in a position to receive the report and brief the government on the contents of it in the week commencing April 7, and I expect therefore that the report will be able to be released sometime during that week," Costello told parliament.
The inquiry, established by the government and headed by prominent businessman Stan Wallis, is the first major review of Australian finance sector regulations since the early 1980s.
Its wide-ranging report is expected to include a recommendation to end the current "six pillars" policy which prevent mergers between the four big Australian banks and the two largest life offices.
Analysts also expect it to recommend that mergers be determined by the anti-monopoly authority rather than by the government ad hoc.
"The government will, of course, announce its attitude towards the report at the time of release," Costello said.

"There may be some things that the government responds to straight away and there will unquestionably be a number of things that it will take some time for the government to develop a position on and announce a response."
Costello said he wanted to remind companies that might be affected by the report that current policies remained in place until changes were announced.
"Any person that takes a commercial decision in the interim does so at their own risk," he said.
Shares in both Westpac Banking Corp and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd have risen sharply in recent days on speculation that the release of the report was imminent.

Both banks are seen as potential takeover targets if the report recommends permitting bank mega-mergers and the government accepts any such recommendation. National Australia Bank Ltd, the largest and most profitable of the major banks, is seen as the most likely buyer.
At 2.50 p.m. (0350 GMT), Westpac shares were four cents higher at A$7.53, but ANZ shares were five cents lower at A$8.23 after earlier reaching a high of A$8.41.
